Consider the collection of point masses above, where the $x$-coordinates are measured in meters. What is the $x$-coordinate of the center of mass for this system?

feedback.problem: Consider the collection of point masses ${m}_{1}=3\,\text{kg},$ ${m}_{2}=6\,\text{kg},$ ${m}_{3}=1\,\text{kg},$ and ${m}_{4}=5\,\text{kg}$ located at ${x}_{1}=-2,$ ${x}_{2}=2.5,$ ${x}_{3}=1,$ and ${x}_{4}=4,$ respectively, along the $x$-axis, where the $x$-coordinates are measured in meters. What is the $x$-coordinate of the center of mass for this system?
feedback.worked_solution:
The center of mass, denoted $\overset{―}{x},$ of a collection of point masses ${m}_{1},{m}_{2},…,{m}_{n}$ located at ${x}_{1},{x}_{2},…,{x}_{n}$ along the $x$-axis is given by 

$$
\overset{―}{x}=\frac{{M}_{O}}{m},
$$

 

where 

- $m={\sum }_{i=1}^{n}{m}_{i}$ is the total mass of the system,

- ${M}_{O}={\sum }_{i=1}^{n}{m}_{i}{x}_{i}$ is the total moment of the system about the origin $O.$

In our case, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{m}_{1} & =3, & \,{m}_{2} & =6, & \,{m}_{3} & =1, & \,{m}_{4} & =5, \\ {x}_{1} & =-2, & \,{x}_{2} & =2.5, & \,{x}_{3} & =1, & \,{x}_{4} & =4.\end{aligned}
$$

So, the total mass of the system is

$$
\begin{aligned}m & ={\sum }_{i=1}^{n}{m}_{i} \\  & ={m}_{1}+{m}_{2}+{m}_{3} \\  & =3+6+1+5 \\  & =15\,\text{kg}\end{aligned}
$$

and the moment of the system about the origin is

$$
\begin{aligned}{M}_{O} & ={\sum }_{i=1}^{n}{m}_{i}{x}_{i} \\  & ={m}_{1}{x}_{1}+{m}_{2}{x}_{2}+{m}_{3}{x}_{3}+{m}_{4}{x}_{4} \\  & =3\cdot (-2)+6\cdot 2.5+1\cdot 1+5\cdot 4 \\  & =-6+15+1+20 \\  & =30\,\text{kg}\cdot \text{m}.\end{aligned}
$$

 

Therefore, 

$$
\overset{―}{x}=\frac{{M}_{O}}{m}=\frac{30}{15}=2.
$$
